join.q: How do I become a member?
join.a: Fill the membership form on the Join page with your details and photo. Our team reviews every application.

status.q: I have applied. How do I know if I am approved?
status.a: Open the "Check status" page and enter your mobile number and date of birth. It shows whether your application is under review or approved.

card.q: How do I get my membership card?
card.a: Once you are approved, your membership card opens from the "Check status" page. You can print it at ID-card size and laminate it. If you gave an email, the card is also emailed to you.

volunteer.q: How can I become a volunteer?
volunteer.a: Fill the volunteer form and choose how you would like to help. Our team will contact you.

problem.q: I have a problem and need the organisation's help. What do I do?
problem.a: Raise a request at the help desk. You get a reference number to follow up on it.

donate.q: How can I support the organisation with a donation?
donate.a: Use the Donate page to give online. You get a receipt for your donation.

help.intro: Facing caste discrimination, an atrocity or injustice? Tell us. Our team will reach out to help.

help.stationHint: Important for this kind of complaint. Write the name of the police station.

help.voiceHint: Hard to type? Speak and tell us what happened (up to 3 minutes).
help.voiceNoSupport: Voice recording does not work in this browser. Please write instead.
help.voiceDenied: Please allow the microphone to record a voice message.
help.photosHint: Up to 3 photos. For example a photo of the incident, an FIR copy or an application.
help.rightsIntro: What the police and the law must do for you
help.rightsNote: This is general information, not legal advice. Our team can guide you on your case.

rights.fir: For a serious (cognisable) offence, the police must register an FIR. You can ask for a free copy of it.
rights.zero: You can file an FIR at any police station, even if the incident happened in another area (Zero FIR).
rights.sp: If the police station refuses, give your complaint in writing to the Superintendent of Police (SP) of the district, or go to the court (magistrate).
rights.duty: Under the SC/ST (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, a government servant (who is not SC/ST) who wilfully neglects their duty under the Act, such as not registering your complaint, can be punished.
rights.relief: Victims of atrocities are entitled to relief money and support from the government under this Act.
rights.copies: Keep a copy of every application you give. Note the date and the name of the officer.
